title: [AUTHORED — not exercised by the public sample] READU...LOCKED retry-or-fail pattern with explicit RELEASE
sourceContent:
* reserve-stock.pick - reserve inventory under an exclusive lock
PGM = 'VZ.RESERVE.STOCK'
OPEN 'STOCK' TO STK ELSE
   STOP
END

READU QTY.REC FROM STK, ITEM.ID LOCKED
   PRINT 'Item locked by another user, retry later.'
   RETURN
END ELSE
   PRINT 'Item not found: ':ITEM.ID
   RETURN
END

ON.HAND = QTY.REC<1>
IF ON.HAND < REQUESTED THEN
   RELEASE STK, ITEM.ID
   PRINT 'Insufficient stock.'
   RETURN
END

QTY.REC<1> = ON.HAND - REQUESTED
WRITE QTY.REC ON STK, ITEM.ID
RELEASE STK, ITEM.ID
RETURN
notes: AUTHORED — the small public calibration sample (github.com/zelenko/pick) does not exercise record locking, so this entry is written to represent a well-documented, universal UniBasic/MultiValue concept (READU...LOCKED / RELEASE) rather than derived from real client or public code. A genuine client engagement must validate the exact locking semantics against the client's real UniData source. READU with the LOCKED clause is the pessimistic-read-lock idiom; RELEASE explicitly drops it — maps to a JPA @Lock(PESSIMISTIC_WRITE) transaction in the Java target.
